occlusion_visible_intervals — DRIVE traffic op

• Data kinds: any → any

• Call: import fullseye as fs; fs.ledger.occlusion_visible_intervals(ego_xy, ego_heading: 'float', parked_box, emerge_xy, s_max: 'float') -> 'list' (to call the implementation directly, import drivetraffic; drivetraffic.occlusion_visible_intervals(ego_xy, ego_heading: 'float', parked_box, emerge_xy, s_max: 'float') -> 'list'; from the registry, opsdrive.get("occlusion_visible_intervals"))

Usage

While the ego vehicle's eye advances along p(s) = ego_xy + s h for 0 ≤ s ≤ s_max, the list of intervals of advance during which the point emerge_xy is visible.

occlusion_reveal_distance returns only "the first place where it becomes visible", but visibility is not monotonic: a point outside the band of the parked vehicle's width (on the pavement) is visible from afar through the gap between the car and the kerb, becomes hidden as one approaches, and becomes visible again. Here [0, s_max] is split at the candidates where visible/not visible can switch (intersections of corner-grazing lines of sight with the path, intersections of the path with the edges —— closed form), the line of sight is tested at the midpoint of each interval, and the visible intervals are returned as [(s0, s1), ...] (ascending, adjacent visible intervals merged). The longitudinal distance at an interval end is h · (e − p(s)). If the point is inside the box, [].

Raises ValueError: shape, non-finite, dimension ≤ 0, s_max ≤ 0.
